title: Shopping starts with AI and demand is cautious: make our store agent-ready
summary: 55% of consumers use AI in product discovery (NIQ); Google launched Universal Cart; Newegg added Google UCP checkout; Amex launched an agent-purchase framework. Q3 PC shipments fell over 20% (DigiTimes); Circana sees flat holiday spend.

points.headline: AI is becoming a mainstream way to discover products
points.detail: 55% of consumers use AI in discovery (NIQ) and 34% of US consumers would use GenAI for holiday gift ideas (Gartner). We should make our catalog AI-readable and track AI-referred traffic.

points.headline: Agent checkout is going live across Google, Newegg and Amex
points.detail: Google opened Universal Cart in Search and Gemini, Newegg added Google UCP checkout, and Amex published a framework for agent purchases. We should assess our readiness for agent-led purchases.

points.headline: PC demand is weak while memory costs stay high
points.detail: Global PC shipments fell over 20% year over year in Q3, and AI data center demand keeps DRAM and NAND prices rising into Q4. We should plan holiday stock and pricing carefully.

points.headline: Holiday online sales grow, but shoppers stay value-driven
points.detail: Adobe forecasts record US online holiday sales of $275.1B (+6.7%), while Circana expects overall spending between down 1% and up 2.5%. We should lead with price and convenience in Cyber 5 plans.
